summary: Daily prorated reserve credit appears shifted to previous UTC day after delayed postback
summary_detail: Customer reports that a daily prorated reserve credit (applied for reserved capacity) was posted to the previous UTC day on their invoice, causing a shortfall on the expected credits for 2026-03-11. They observed the application after running an hourly batch and seeing a late postback arrival at ~00:20 UTC on 2026-03-12.
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NarrativeAI noticed a missing prorated reserved capacity credit for their 2026-03-11 usage. The reserve credit appears on the account but attached to 2026-03-10 (previous UTC day). Impact: customer sees a $1,200 provisional shortfall and is concerned about final invoice reconciliation.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east)
- Customer on Enterprise reserved plan with hourly reserve buffer
- Several batch jobs running in local timezone America/Los_Angeles (UTC-8/UTC-7 depending on DST)

Impact:
- Temporary invoice imbalance and alerting from customer finance team
- Potential automated billing hold if not resolved before next billing run

Why this is suspicious:
- Customer's internal logs show the reserve reconciliation postback arrived at 2026-03-12T00:20:16Z, but our billing ledger tagged the credit to 2026-03-10 rather than 2026-03-11.
- The gap correlates with a known short-duration postback rate-limiter behaviour introduced in 2026-02 release (rate-limiter backfill window adjusted).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Run an hourly reserved-capacity batch job from customer zone (America/Los_Angeles) that finishes near midnight local time.
2) Force the charge reconciliation to emit a postback (simulate network delay by holding for ~20 minutes).
3) Observe the postback ingestion timestamp in billing-ingest and which day the prorate credit is allocated to in ledger-service.
logs: Ledger write: credit_id=CR-78910 allocated_to_day=2026-03-10 user_org=NarrativeAI amount=-1200.00
Rate-limiter trace: rate-limiter.backfill_window=48h (config change on 2026-02-27), fallback path triggered due to transient datastore timeout
investigation_notes: Initial triage by support: flagged as likely ledger allocation bug where ingestion uses 'event_generation_day' derived from local processing timezone rather than 'postback.sent_time' UTC.
Billing-engineer (Priya) looked at ledger-service code paths: found a code branch that uses 'ingest_slot_day = floor(ingest_time - ingest_offset)' when postback.sent_time is missing or flagged stale.
hypotheses_tested: H1: Late postback ingestion caused the backfill window code to rebucket the credit to start_of_day(ingest_time-48h) resulting in two-day shift. Test: reingest the original postback with original headers -> repro on staging.

H2: Timezone conversion bug where America/Los_Angeles DST boundary produced off-by-one when converting local job completion to UTC day. Test: replay jobs across DST boundary - no repro; H2 deprioritized.

H3: Race condition between rate-limiter backfill eviction and ledger idempotency window causing previous day's bucket to be reused. Test: add deterministic timestamp override in staging to observe behavior.
Current status: H1 reproduced in staging using a replayed postback with an artificial 27-minute ingestion delay.
comments: 2026-03-12 | Aisha Patel (Support): Contacted customer to acknowledge issue and requested full raw postback payload + headers. Asked for a playback window +/- 1 hour around the job end time.

2026-03-12 | Morgan Li (Billing Eng): Assigned to investigate ledger allocation. Noted potential linkage to rate-limiter backfill change from Feb release. Will attempt a safe reingest of original payload to see where it lands.
2026-03-12 | Customer (Danielle, NarrativeAI): Provided signed postback payload and said accounting needs a provisional waiver if not fixed by 2026-03-15 billing run.

2026-03-13 | Priya Shah (Systems): Reingested payload in staging; reproduced allocation to previous day. Root cause narrowed to billing-ingest using 'processed_day = floor(now_utc - backfill_window)' when 'sent_time' header was present but not parsed because of new header format (microseconds field).

2026-03-13 | Morgan Li (Billing Eng): Created fix branch to prefer 'postback.sent_time' if present and only fall back to ingest_time. Opened PR: github.com/redwood-inference/billing-reconciler/pull/421. Adding ledger migration script to move misallocated credits for affected orgs.

2026-03-13 | Support (Aisha): Notified customer of root cause and temporary mitigation (we will run a targeted ledger-adjust migration and reissue provisional credits). Customer requested confirmation once credits appear on 2026-03-13 ledger snapshot.
action_items: 1) Apply hotfix to billing-ingest to parse postback.sent_time microsecond format and favour it over ingest_time (Morgan/Priya) - ETA 2026-03-14.
2) Run one-off ledger migration to move credits from 2026-03-10 -> 2026-03-11 for NarrativeAI (billing team) - ETA 2026-03-13 close-of-day.
3) Add a test in reconciliation-suite to simulate delayed postbacks and ensure no day-shift regressions (QA/Eng).
4) Notify Finance and Customer Success and issue provisional waiver if migration cannot complete before 2026-03-15 billing run (Support Manager).
resolution: Mitigation executed: billing team ran a ledger migration that reallocated CR-78910 and two related credits to 2026-03-11. Hotfix merged to billing-reconciler (PR 421) to prioritise postback.sent_time parsing. Additional reconciliation test merged to CI. Customer confirmed provisional balance corrected on 2026-03-13 ledger snapshot.
final_status: Resolved - credits reallocated and hotfix deployed to prod; follow-up tests added to prevent recurrence
postmortem_follow_up: Schedule postmortem with Billing, SRE, and Support to review backfill_window config change and why tests didn't cover microsecond header format - target 2026-03-20.
Update Confluence runbook to document ordering: prefer postback.sent_time, then ingest_time; include header formats to accept.
Notify customers on enterprise reserved plans who had jobs finishing within +/- 1 hour of UTC day boundary in the Feb 27 - Mar 12 window for potential credit misallocations.
